info.bio:
Existen 2 bandas llamadas Poison:

1) Banda estadounidense de Glam Metal.

2) Banda alemana de Thrash/Death Metal. 


1. La banda estadounidense nació en el año 1983 en Harrisburg, Pensilvania (Estados Unidos); lugar donde se conocieron sus integrantes originales y fundadores Bret Michaels (vocalista) y Rikki Rockett (bateria), a los que posteriormente se unieron Matt Smith (guitarra) y Bobby Dall (bajo). Antes de que saliera su album debut Smith dejo el grupo y fue reemplazado por C.C. DeVille.

scenes.name: Lite metal: pop metal y glam
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El subgénero que, desde 1983-84, intensifica el polo melódico del heavy y lo mezcla con el hard rock, quitándole el grave grueso. Philip Bashe lo llamó «metal pop» y señaló a Def Leppard y Van Halen; otros ejemplos son Poison, Bon Jovi, Ratt y Cinderella. Sus detractores, el público tradicional y el del thrash, lo llaman «poseurs», «false metal», «nerf metal», «poodle bands» o «glam», motes que describen bien sus rasgos: falta de autenticidad, pelo cardado, ropa colorida en lugar del negro obrero. Voz dulce sin gruñidos, armonías al modo de Aerosmith y Kiss, letras de amor y lujuria con nombres de chica y, sobre todo, la power ballad, que entra en radios que excluían el heavy y gana público nuevo, como las versiones blancas de Pat Boone en los cincuenta. MTV impulsó mucho su desarrollo. Se queda con la herencia dionisíaca y elimina el caos: «lo realmente pesado se quita».
scenes.family: Lite metal: glam y pop metal

scenes.name: El oficio: del air guitar al dios del metal
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El músico de heavy sale del público: es el fan que toca la guitarra de aire en el concierto de UFO de 1979 y quiere estar donde está Michael Schenker. No hay escuela ni beca: hace falta talento musical y dramático (actuar la emoción por trescientas veces), un cuerpo joven y atlético (correr y pesas en la gira, el pelo largo como signo de autenticidad) y aprender a vivir en un grupo que no es ni familia ni oficina, con sus «problemas de ego» por la rivalidad entre cantante y guitarrista. El heavy es el estilo más caro de montar y casi no hay clubes donde empezar; el código exige temas propios y autenticidad. Firmar con un sello convierte a la banda en una empresa del capitalismo tardío frente a un oligopolio. El ciclo es componer, grabar (paciencia; el primer disco de Black Sabbath se hizo en doce horas, Spreading the Disease de Anthrax en cinco meses) y girar (aguante: esperar, esperar). La recompensa no es el dinero sino el carisma del chamán que alcanza el éxtasis dionisíaco ante miles de personas; el precio, «quemarse o apagarse», porque nadie que viva lo bastante puede cumplir el código.

scenes.name: MTV y Headbangers Ball
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: MTV nace en agosto de 1981 y en dos años casi monopoliza el videoclip. El heavy, visual desde que Judas Priest se vistió de cuero, es un candidato natural: entre los primeros grupos emitidos están Quiet Riot, Mötley Crüe, Twisted Sister, Dokken y Scorpions, y la cuota de mercado del metal salta del 8 % en 1983 al 20 % en 1984 («MTV fue responsable del resurgir del heavy», dice Dee Snider). A principios de 1985 la presión fundamentalista lo recorta, pero en 1988 nace el programa nocturno «Headbangers Ball». MTV selecciona del metal lo compatible con un público juvenil general: hace del lite metal un coautor del género (pelo cardado, chico malo mono, chicas en el público) y empuja al thrash, casi ausente, a definirse como antítesis comercial. Los vídeos, rodados por directores de publicidad, cuestan cada vez más (190.000 dólares uno de Poison en 1989) y dejan fuera a las bandas pequeñas, convierten los conciertos en simulacros del vídeo y, al llevar el metal al salón familiar, despiertan a sus enemigos: la lista de los «Filthy Fifteen» del PMRC y el departamento de normas de MTV.
scenes.family: Cultura metal: público, medios y conciertos

scenes.name: Vídeos y cine: de The Song Remains the Same a Spinal Tap
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Fuera de MTV el vídeo es un medio especializado que los fans compran: recopilaciones (Fuel for Life de Judas Priest), conciertos (Live After Death de Iron Maiden), documentales al modo de The Song Remains the Same de Led Zeppelin, cintas-revista y promociones de sellos independientes de thrash como Combat y Metal Blade. Metallica deconstruye el formato con Cliff ’em All, homenaje a Cliff Burton hecho con grabaciones caseras y piratas. El cine, que necesita un público de masas, apenas trata el metal, salvo como banda sonora de películas de terror. Las dos películas sobre él de los ochenta, This Is Spinal Tap (1984), la parodia de Rob Reiner, y The Decline of Western Civilization Part II: The Metal Years (1988) de Penelope Spheeris, dan placer al público metal pero aún más a sus detractores: una es una crítica cultural de la falta de sofisticación; la otra, una crítica moral de la depravación, estrenada tras los ataques del PMRC. Spinal Tap acabó saliendo de gira de verdad.

podcast.title: Decline of "Cheesy Pop Metal" (1991)
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis, in his autobiography "Scar Tissue," identified Poison as one of the "cheesy pop metal bands" that were "finished" by 1991, signaling a changing of the musical guard. "Cheesy pop metal bands like Warren's and Poison and Skid Row were finished."

podcast.title: "New Rockers" (Late 1980s)
podcast.body: Identified as one of the "new rockers" of the late 1980s, characterized by "more flash than substance," during a period when pop music was dominant. "The new rockers, Poison, Motley Crew, Quiet Rhyth, were really more flash than substance."

srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14

podcast.title: CC Deville's Alleged Contact with U2
podcast.body: An uncorroborated rumor suggests that Poison guitarist CC Deville was contacted by U2 in the early 1990s to act as their backup guitarist for the *Achtung Baby* album and the Zoo TV tour. Deville was allegedly flattered but turned down the offer, citing a desire "not to compromise his musical integrity." Furthermore, alleged quotes from Bono and The Edge are presented, praising Deville's guitar work and crediting Poison as inspiration for U2's visual choices during the *Achtung Baby* era.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: CC Deville's Alleged Uncredited Work with U2
podcast.body: A rumor, supposedly revealed by Poison's singer, claims that CC Deville played lead guitar on U2's song "Mysterious Ways" but did not receive credit. This lack of credit was allegedly to protect Deville's image, and Poison's singer reportedly exposed this secret to ensure Deville's fans knew he "hung around with a bunch of note talent, Wussys."

xref.title: Meeting and Formation (Sacramento 1972-1975)
xref.body: Erick perkaiser (Lux interior) and Kristi Marlena Wallace (Poison Ivy) met in Sacramento in 1972. They were drawn together by a shared passion for horror movies and record collecting. By 1975, they had formed The Cramps and began performing at venues like CBGB, sharing stages with bands such as The Ramones, Blondie, Talking Heads, and Patti Smith. "They met in Sacramento back in 1972, and were drawn together by their love of horror movies and record collecting. By 1975, they'd formed the Cramps and were playing places like CBGB alongside their hormones and blondie and talking heads and patty smith and so many others."

xref.title: Enduring Core (Until 2006)
xref.body: While other members of The Cramps changed over time, Lux interior and Poison Ivy remained a constant, together recording and performing until 2006. "Other members of the Cramps came and went, but Lux and Poison Ivy stayed together recording and performing until 2006."

xref.title: Lux Interior's Death (February 4, 2009)
xref.body: Lux interior died suddenly on February 4, 2009, from an aortic dissection, an undiagnosed condition where the body's largest artery ruptures, leading to rapid internal bleeding. He and Poison Ivy had been married for 37 years. "But then on February 4th, 2009, Lux suddenly died after suffering an aortic dissection, an undiagnosed condition where your aorta, the largest artery in your body, bursts, and you bleed out internally in seconds."

xref.title: Absence of a Bass Player
xref.body: In the band's early days, The Cramps did not have a bass player, leaving it entirely up to guitarist Poison Ivy to handle the low-end duties and anchor the music. "Early on, the band didn't have a bass player. It was entirely up to Ivy to hold things down."

xref.title: Band's End with Lux Interior's Death
xref.body: The Cramps disbanded after the death of singer Lux Interior in 2009 from an undiagnosed cardiovascular condition. Lux and Poison Ivy had been together for 37 years. "until Lux died of an undiagnosed cardiovascular condition in 2009. Now is the end of the band. Lux and Ivy had been together for 37 years."

xref.title: Cult Status and Influence
xref.body: The Cramps, with Poison Ivy at its core alongside her husband and frontman Lux Interior, became a cult favorite that continues to influence subsequent generations of guitarists, both male and female, as evidenced by bands like Queens of the Stone Age. "And in the process, the Cranps became this weird cult favorite that is still having an impact today. As Queens of the Stone Age, what they think of Ivy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: Poison Ivy, whose real name is Kristi Marlena Wallace, originated from California and began playing the guitar at an early age. "She was originally from California and started playing the guitar early."

xref.title: Extensive Production Success
xref.body: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, Fairbairn produced mega-platinum albums for numerous major rock bands, including Aerosmith, AC/DC, Bon Jovi, INXS, Kiss, Loverboy, Poison, The Scorpions, and Van Halen, accumulating close to 100 million album sales. "Throughout the 80s and 90s, he produced mega platinum albums for Erasmith and ACDC and Bon Jovi and Inaccess and Kiss and Leverboy and Poison, The Scorpions and Van Halen and a ton of others."

xref.title: Musical Style and Contribution to The Cramps
xref.body: Poison Ivy, real name Christie Wallace, was the guitarist and co-writer of all original songs for The Cramps, a New York City-based band known for its unique blend of punk, psychobilly, garage, and horror movie aesthetics. She also occasionally provided vocals and, despite not being a virtuoso, was an inspirational figure in a challenging music scene. "She co-wrote all the groups original songs and occasionally sang."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Poison Ivy's Guitar Influence
xref.body: Poison Ivy's distinctive guitar style was considered a crucial influence on various aspects of the punk rock music scene. "Her guitar style was seen as an essential influence on certain areas of the punk rock universe."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Manchester Pigeon Massacre
xref.body: Growing up in Manchester, Shaun Ryder harbored a strong dislike for pigeons. After an incident where birds tried to steal his Kentucky Fried Chicken, he exacted revenge, claiming to have caused about 3,000 pigeons to fall from the sky over Manchester through conflicting methods such as feeding them rat poison or tiny rocks of crack, meth, or ecstasy. "Anyway, by the time he was done, Sean says that about 3,000 pigeons fell from the sky over Manchester."
